{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]] | [[Cookbook:Meat Recipes|Meat Recipes]]

The word ''teriyaki'' is a combination of two Japanese words, ''teri'', "luster", and ''yaki'', "to grill or broil". The [[Cookbook:Mirin|mirin]] in the sauce gives a good luster to meat as it is cooked. Traditionally it was used with fish. It can also be used as a [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinade]] for pre-cooked meat and poultry, as well as a delicious [[Cookbook:Basting|baste]] for items on the grill or rotisserie. Teriyaki sauce is a complement to virtually any type of meat (as long as you adjust the flavors accordingly), especially steak, chicken, fish and pork.

==Ingredients==

* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (2 parts) [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* ¼ cup (2 parts) [[Cookbook:Mirin|mirin]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (1 part) [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 tsp fresh, peeled, finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 1 tsp fresh, peeled, finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* A litte bit of [[Cookbook:Sake|sake]] (optional)
==Procedure==

#Mix everything in a 1-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] pot over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
#Use sauce to [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] some raw meat or vegetables overnight in the refrigerator.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*As given, this sauce is thin. [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] 1/2 tsp [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]] or [[Cookbook:Potato Starch|potato starch]] or kuzu root starch (for Japanese authenticity) into it if you wish to thicken it.
*[[Cookbook:Pineapple|Pineapple]] juice might be a reasonable [[Cookbook:Mirin|mirin]] substitute.
*Lime juice may also be added for a tart flavor.
